title: GC age metric mismatch: gc.rs uses date_ms but candidates selected on ingested_at_ms
description:
## What / Why
In crates/transit/src/retention/gc.rs, run_once() logs GC decisions using candidate.date_ms (the article's Date: header timestamp). But gc_candidates.rs selects candidates based on ingested_at_ms (wall-clock ingestion time). These are different values: an old article ingested recently passes the ingested_at_ms grace period but its date_ms may be far in the past, causing misleading age calculations in GC decisions and audit log entries.

## Trigger → Bad Behavior
An article with Date: from 2020 ingested today: gc_candidates selects it only after the grace period from ingestion, but gc.rs logs it as '4+ years old' based on the 2020 Date header. If any future code path uses date_ms for policy decisions rather than ingested_at_ms, old articles could be GC'd prematurely regardless of their ingestion recency.

## Fix
Use a single time basis (ingested_at_ms) consistently throughout GC selection and logging. Alternatively, if article age by Date: header is intentional for display, document the distinction explicitly with a comment explaining both fields and when each is appropriate.
